sections.d: Spouse and children shape everything else.
Changes federal estate tax rules for your spouse.

questions.q: Your full legal name
questions.why: Documents must use your exact legal name.

questions.q: Which state do you live in?
questions.why: Signing rules, taxes and forms differ by state.

questions.q: Marital status
questions.why: Spouses have legal rights that wills must respect.

questions.q: Spouse's full legal name
questions.why: Named as primary beneficiary and often as agent.

questions.q: Do you have children? (pick all that apply)
questions.why: Minors need a guardian and a trust; special needs need a supplemental trust.

questions.q: Children's full names and birth dates
questions.why: Naming every child avoids a claim of being left out.

questions.q: Your citizenship
questions.why: The estate tax exemption depends on citizenship and domicile.

questions.q: Your spouse's citizenship
questions.why: A non-citizen spouse can't use the unlimited marital deduction.

questions.q: Do you intend to stay in the U.S. indefinitely?
questions.why: Intent to stay is what makes you a U.S. domiciliary for estate tax.

questions.q: What do you own?
questions.why: Some assets pass by beneficiary form, not by will.

questions.q: Which countries, and what kind of assets?
questions.why: A separate local will is often best for foreign property.

questions.q: Rough total of everything (incl. life insurance)
questions.why: Decides whether federal or state estate tax could matter.

questions.q: Would you like a revocable living trust to avoid probate?
questions.why: A living trust keeps assets out of probate and private.

questions.q: Executor (and backup)
questions.why: Settles your estate and pays debts.

questions.q: Guardian for minor children (and backup)
questions.why: The court gives great weight to your nomination.

questions.q: Does your first-choice guardian live outside the U.S.?
questions.why: Name a U.S.-based backup and trustee.

questions.q: Trustee for the children's money
questions.why: Can be different from the guardian.

questions.q: Age the children get full control
questions.why: Without a trust they inherit outright at the age of majority.

questions.q: Financial power of attorney agent (and backup)
questions.why: Handles money if you can't.

questions.q: Healthcare agent (and backup)
questions.why: Makes medical decisions if you can't.

questions.q: Who gets everything else?
questions.why: The residue clause covers everything not specifically gifted.

questions.q: If terminally ill or permanently unconscious
questions.why: Goes into your living will / advance directive.

questions.q: Organ donor?
questions.why: Recorded in your advance directive.

questions.q: Pet caretaker and amount for pet care
questions.why: Most states allow an enforceable pet trust.
